title: The Bus Lane Puzzle: Correlation or Cause?
instructions: 阅读一篇关于城市交通研究的模拟材料（所有数据均为虚构，仅用于教学）。先通读文章，理解研究小组如何区分相关与因果。然后完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、匹配、判断）。最后学习语法“倍数与比例表达；比较结构；过去和现在数据的时态选择”，并完成8道语法题。注意：填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
passage:
A research group at a city university wanted to understand why traffic on Maple Avenue had become slower over a period of five years. The team, led by Dr. Chen, collected data from 2018 and 2023. They measured average travel time, bus passenger numbers, and the number of cars on the road. The results were surprising and challenged what many people believed.

In 2018, the average car trip along Maple Avenue took 18 minutes. By 2023, the same trip took 27 minutes. That is one and a half times longer than before. During the same period, the number of cars on the road rose from 12,000 per day to 18,000 per day. At the same time, the city added a bus lane in 2021. Some people said the bus lane caused the delay. They argued that fewer car lanes meant more congestion, so cars had to move more slowly.

Dr. Chen's team looked more carefully at the situation. They found that the bus lane actually carried more people than a car lane. A bus lane moved about 3,000 passengers per hour, while a car lane moved only 1,200 people per hour. This means the bus lane was two and a half times more efficient at moving people. However, the team also noticed that the number of cars had increased by 50% since 2018. This rise happened before the bus lane was built, so the bus lane could not be the reason for the earlier growth in traffic. The team concluded that the bus lane was not the main cause of slower traffic. The real cause was the growing number of cars.

To test this idea, the researchers compared Maple Avenue with Oak Street, which had no bus lane. Oak Street also saw a 50% increase in cars, and its travel time rose from 15 to 22 minutes. This was similar to what happened on Maple Avenue. The team said, "Correlation is not causation. Just because two things happen together does not mean one causes the other." In other words, two events can happen at the same time without one being the reason for the other.

The city now plans to add more bus lanes and also to improve traffic lights. Dr. Chen advises: "We need to look at the data carefully. A bus lane can be good for the city even if cars are slower." This shows that a measure like a bus lane can help many people travel efficiently, even when car drivers experience longer trips.

grammar.title: 倍数与比例表达；比较结构；过去和现在数据的时态选择
grammar.explanation: 在描述数据时，我们常用倍数和比例。例如：one and a half times longer（长一倍半），two and a half times more efficient（效率高两倍半）。比较结构常用 than，如 more people than a car lane。描述过去的数据用一般过去时（In 2018, it took 18 minutes），描述现在的数据用一般现在时（The city now plans...）。注意区分：新学的“倍数+比较级”结构（如 three times faster）与复习的简单比较级（如 faster than）。
grammar.example: That is one and a half times longer.

questions.prompt: The new train is ______ than the old bus. (fast)
questions.evidence: That is one and a half times longer.

questions.prompt: This road is ______ than that one. (wide)
questions.evidence: two and a half times more efficient

questions.explanation: 过去数据用一般过去时：was。
questions.evidence: In 2018, the average car trip along Maple Avenue took 18 minutes.

questions.explanation: 现在数据用一般现在时：has。
questions.evidence: The city now plans to add more bus lanes

questions.prompt: The bus lane moves ______ people than a car lane. (many)
questions.explanation: 比较级用 more people than。
questions.evidence: the bus lane actually carried more people than a car lane

questions.prompt: Last year, the number of cars ______ by 20%. (rise)
questions.explanation: 过去数据用一般过去时：rose。
questions.evidence: The number of cars on the road rose from 12,000 per day to 18,000 per day.

questions.prompt: This year, the travel time ______ 30 minutes. (be)
questions.explanation: 现在数据用一般现在时：is。
questions.evidence: By 2023, the same trip took 27 minutes.

questions.prompt: The new system is ______ than the old one. (good)
questions.evidence: A bus lane can be good for the city
